## Appendix: notation at a glance {#notation data-menu-title="Appendix: notation"}

| Symbol | Meaning | In the kidney-stone example |
|:-------------|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| $T$ | Treatment: $1$ = treated, $0$ = control | $T = 1$: open surgery (A); $T = 0$: keyhole (B) |
| $Y$ | Outcome | $Y = 1$ if the treatment succeeded |
| $X$ | Observed covariates, measured before treatment | Stone size: small (under 2 cm) or large (2 cm or more) |
| $U$ | An unobserved variable | Frailty the doctor saw but never recorded |
| $Y(1),\ Y(0)$ | Potential outcomes: $Y$ *if* treated, *if* not (Pearl writes $y_t$ for $Y(t)$) | Success had the patient got A; had they got B |
| $\tau$ | Causal effect $Y(1) - Y(0)$ (for patient $i$: $\tau_i$) | Did A make the difference for this patient? |
| $\operatorname{do}(T = t)$ | Intervention: *set* $T$ to $t$ | "Give every patient treatment A" |
| $e(x)$ | Propensity score $\mathbb{P}(T = 1 \mid X = x)$ | $\mathbb{P}(\text{A} \mid \text{small}) = 87/357 = 0.24$ |
| $\mu_t(x)$ | Outcome regression $\mathbb{E}[Y \mid T = t, X = x]$ | Success rate of A on small stones: $0.93$ |

[Also: $M$ mediator and $C$ collider (Section 3), $Z$ instrument (Section 5). $T \perp\!\!\!\perp Y \mid X$ means "$T$ and $Y$ are independent given $X$". Linked from the Roadmap; the menu (press **M**) jumps here too.]{.small .muted}

::: {.notes}
A reference slide, not one to teach. It collects every symbol used in the deck, with its kidney-stone meaning: T, Y, X are always treatment, outcome, and observed covariates (stone size); Y(1) and Y(0) are the two potential outcomes of Section 2, of which we only ever see one. Pearl's counterfactual notation y_t from the ladder of causation is the same object as Y(t). The numbers in the last column come from the 700 patients: P(A | small) = 87/357 = 0.24 is the propensity score of Section 4, and 81/87 = 0.93 is the success rate of A on small stones.
:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
mulberry32 = (seed) => {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    a |= 0; a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) | 0;
    let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
    t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}
randn = (rng) => { let u = 0; while (u === 0) u = rng(); return Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(u)) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * rng()); }
expit = (x) => 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-x))
dnorm = (z) => Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z) / Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)
pnorm = (z) => {
  // Abramowitz–Stegun 26.2.17
  const t = 1 / (1 + 0.2316419 * Math.abs(z));
  const p = dnorm(z) * t * (0.31938153 + t * (-0.356563782 + t * (1.781477937 + t * (-1.821255978 + t * 1.330274429))));
  return z >= 0 ? 1 - p : p;
}
qnorm = (p) => {
  let lo = -10, hi = 10;
  for (let i = 0; i < 80; i++) { const mid = (lo + hi) / 2; if (pnorm(mid) < p) lo = mid; else hi = mid; }
  return (lo + hi) / 2;
}
solveLin = (A, b) => {
  const n = b.length, M = A.map((r, i) => [...r, b[i]]);
  for (let c = 0; c < n; c++) {
    let p = c; for (let r = c + 1; r < n; r++) if (Math.abs(M[r][c]) > Math.abs(M[p][c])) p = r;
    [M[c], M[p]] = [M[p], M[c]];
    for (let r = 0; r < n; r++) if (r !== c) { const f = M[r][c] / M[c][c]; for (let k = c; k <= n; k++) M[r][k] -= f * M[c][k]; }
  }
  return M.map((r, i) => r[n] / r[i]);
}
olsFit = (X, y, w) => {
  const p = X[0].length, A = Array.from({length: p}, () => new Array(p).fill(0)), b = new Array(p).fill(0);
  X.forEach((x, i) => { const wi = w ? w[i] : 1; for (let j = 0; j < p; j++) { b[j] += wi * x[j] * y[i]; for (let k = 0; k < p; k++) A[j][k] += wi * x[j] * x[k]; } });
  return solveLin(A, b);
}
logitFit = (X, y) => {
  let beta = new Array(X[0].length).fill(0);
  for (let it = 0; it < 10; it++) {
    const w = [], z = [];
    X.forEach((x, i) => {
      const eta = x.reduce((s, v, k) => s + v * beta[k], 0), mu = Math.min(1 - 1e-6, Math.max(1e-6, expit(eta))), wi = mu * (1 - mu);
      w.push(wi); z.push(eta + (y[i] - mu) / wi);
    });
    const next = olsFit(X, z, w);
    const delta = next.reduce((m, v, k) => Math.max(m, Math.abs(v - beta[k])), 0);
    beta = next;
    if (delta < 1e-6) break;
  }
  return beta;
}
// Emit an input's value at most once every `delay` ms (avoids recomputing on every slider pixel)
debounce = (input, delay = 250) => Generators.observe(notify => {
  let timer = null, value;
  const inputted = () => {
    if (timer !== null) return;
    notify(value = input.value);
    timer = setTimeout(delayed, delay);
  };
  const delayed = () => { timer = null; if (value !== input.value) notify(value = input.value); };
  input.addEventListener("input", inputted);
  inputted();
  return () => input.removeEventListener("input", inputted);
})
// Quiz helper: quiz(answer, correct, feedback) where feedback maps each option to an explanation.
quiz = (answer, correct, feedback = {}) => answer == null
  ? html`<div class="readout quiz">Choose an answer to see feedback.</div>`
  : html`<div class="readout quiz ${answer === correct ? "good" : "bad"}">${answer === correct ? "✓ <b>Correct.</b> " : "✗ <b>Not quite.</b> "}${feedback[answer] ?? ""}</div>`
```
